task-intent.statement: Pick up an in-flight run at g4-review as a fresh Commander and read my own context headroom before deciding whether to work or hand off.

expected-behavior.statement: The context gauge reported on my first `current` call would describe MY context.

observed-behavior.statement: My first reading was 18 percent (at/over hard) with a TRIP HISTORY of 3, carrying my predecessor's number: gauge.json is written per checklist DIRECTORY, not per agent. After one tool call it read 0.034439 and the trip line vanished.

impact-cost.statement: Four crews in this wave were relaunched into the loop -- read inherited number, trip, hand off, relaunch -- and each cycle was indistinguishable from correct doctrine. I avoided it only because my launch brief carried a hand-written warning.

workaround.statement: Make any tool call, then re-read before believing any gauge number. Filed as issue 477 and under repair in a parallel worktree.

diagnosis.statement: The gauge is keyed to the checklist directory, so identity is inherited rather than established per observing agent.
Key the reading to the observing agent, or refuse to report a reading whose observer identity does not match the caller.

task-intent.statement: Close g4-implement when its implementer tripped hard before writing its own result file.

expected-behavior.statement: A transcribed result would carry the implementer's measurements intact.

observed-behavior.statement: The implementer correctly REFUSED to attest what it had not run, which is the doctrine working. The Commander transcribed instead, and one claim changed meaning in transit: 'only the doctrine test file differs from aa2038d9 outside .agent-work/' is true against the g4 baseline 84d1e998 but false against the fork point, where THREE production paths differ.

impact-cost.statement: Caught by the g4 reviewer and corrected before the PR; the +24 conclusion was unaffected. Cost one review float and one Commander re-derivation.

workaround.statement: The reviewer was told explicitly it was the first independent eyes on those numbers and treated every measurement as a claim. I re-derived with git diff --numstat rather than reasoning about which baseline was meant.

diagnosis.statement: A measurement's baseline is implicit in prose, so across a handoff the frame of reference can swap silently while the sentence stays grammatical.
Transcribed measurements name their baseline ref inline, so a reader can re-run rather than infer it.

task-intent.statement: Close the run's own archive gate after fixing the archive-reachability defect.

expected-behavior.statement: The spine driving this run would carry the repair the run itself produced.

observed-behavior.statement: It does not. This spine was instantiated before g3 landed, so its archive.c2b still holds the pre-fix text with an unsubstituted <branch> placeholder. The engine runs check text through sh -c, where an unquoted < is input redirection: sh tries to open a file named 'branch', exits 1, and gh is never invoked. Always red, in every state of the world.

impact-cost.statement: The final gate of the wave that fixed this defect is blocked BY that defect. Resolved by an Admiral waiver after the substance was real -- branch pushed, PR 516 open -- rather than by improvising.

workaround.statement: Waive on named Admiral authority with the command text and measured exit code recorded verbatim, and state plainly that the check did not pass. Never hand-substitute the branch name to make it green.

diagnosis.statement: A running spine is a snapshot taken at instantiation, so a fix to the template cannot reach instances already in flight.
No remedy proposed -- retrofitting live instances may be worse than the problem. Recorded as an observation, not a rule.

task-intent.statement: Route 14 triage candidates and file the ones that warrant issues.

expected-behavior.statement: The latitude contract classes issue filing as delegated, so filing would be available.

observed-behavior.statement: Class-level delegation, but the TOOL gh issue create is listed pre-clear, annotated 'the gh issue create gap has now recurred four times'. This is the fifth. Delegation of a decision class with no cleared tool is not filing authority.

impact-cost.statement: Nothing filed; 14 issue-ready recommendations handed up instead. The findings are preserved but they are not on the tracker, which is the outcome the human has previously objected to.

workaround.statement: Routed all 14 as recommend-and-defer -- the triage skill's own recorded form of 'ask' -- with a suggested split, and floated the authority gap itself as worth a ruling rather than absorbing it a fifth time.

diagnosis.statement: Decision-class authority and tool-level pre-clearance are recorded in separate tables and can disagree.
Reconcile the two tables, or make the contract state which one wins when they conflict.

task-intent.statement: Run the test suite as the shipped Windows reference instructs.

expected-behavior.statement: references/windows.md section 4 would describe this host correctly.

observed-behavior.statement: It is wrong on this box: it prefers `py`, but `py` has no pytest here, so `py -m pytest` exits nonzero and reads EXACTLY like a red suite when nothing ran.

impact-cost.statement: Cost three crews in this epic real time. A doc that produces a convincing false red is worse than a doc that is merely absent.

workaround.statement: Use `python` always, and never pipe a test command into tail or head -- the exit status then belongs to the pipe, and a zero-match -k selector exits 5 but reads as 0. Redirect to a file and echo the status separately.

diagnosis.statement: The reference generalizes across Windows hosts where the py launcher and the active interpreter differ.
Have the doc tell the reader to verify which interpreter has pytest rather than naming one.
